Copy page Authentication Details Composio-managed OAuth not available OAuth2 Bearer Token Frequently Asked Questions How do I set up OAuth credentials for HighLevel Location? HighLevel Location has no Composio-managed OAuth app, so to connect with OAuth you create your own app in the HighLevel Marketplace. The Location toolkit connects to a single sub-account (HighLevel calls these locations). For agency-wide access, use the HighLevel Agency toolkit instead. Create the HighLevel Marketplace app Sign in to the HighLevel Marketplace with a developer account, click My apps , then click Create app . In the Start from scratch window, set: App name : any name you'll recognize, such as Composio Location . App type : Private for testing and small pilots, or Public if you plan to list the app. Who is the target user of the app? : Sub-Account . The Location toolkit requires this. Who can install the app? : Everyone . Listing type : White-label . Click Create app . Open Advanced Settings > Auth . In Redirect URL , paste https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add and click + Add . It must exactly match the oauth_redirect_uri field in your Composio auth config. On the same page, under Scopes , search for and tick each scope you need, such as locations.readonly . A note like "8 scopes unavailable" is expected: Agency-only scopes are hidden for Sub-Account apps. Open Manage > Secrets . Under Client keys , click + Add , name the key, and click Add . Copy the Client ID and Client secret from the new row. A private app active in more than 5 external agencies can't be installed again until you publish it. Create the auth config in Composio In the Composio dashboard, go to Auth Configs , click Create , and select HighLevel Location (not HighLevel Agency or HighLevel MCP). Name the config, click Next , and choose OAuth 2.0 . Paste the Client id and Client secret , select the same scopes you chose in HighLevel, and click Create Auth Config . Click Connect Account and open the generated link. Sign in to HighLevel, tick the sub-account to connect in Select Sub-Account , click Continue , then click Allow & install . Confirm the account shows as Active . See Custom auth configs for the general flow. Scopes The default auth config requests locations.readonly . Customers approve every scope at install time, so request only what your integration uses. If an action fails with insufficient permissions, add the missing scope in both HighLevel and the auth config, then reconnect. Troubleshooting No sub-accounts listed when connecting : check that the app's target user is Sub-Account and that the HighLevel user you signed in with can access at least one sub-account. Redirect URI mismatch : the URL in HighLevel and in the auth config must be identical. Revoke access In Composio, delete the connected account from the auth config, or disable the auth config. In HighLevel, uninstall the app from the sub-account's installed Marketplace apps. This revokes access immediately.
